# Realistic Vinyl Player

> A turntable in one HTML file. It plays the listener's own audio files in the browser and models a real deck: platter spin-up and coast-down, a pivoted tonearm that tracks across the whole record, pitch that follows platter speed, and generated surface noise. No build step, nothing to install, no network requests; it works offline and from file://.

Everything is in `index.html`: inline CSS and JavaScript, organised by section comments, with all physical constants in one block at the top of the script. A MilkDrop visualizer (butterchurn 2.6.7 with its minimal preset pack, MIT) is inlined unmodified in a separate script block above the player's own; the Visualizer button shows it on the record label, or spectrum bars written after Musializer (MIT), a ridgeline, an oscilloscope, a spectrogram or a radial spectrum. Deck settings hold a Winamp-style ten-band graphic EQ with Winamp's presets (values from Webamp, MIT) and .eqf import, and a Desktop button shows the library as artist and album folders. Audio files, cover art and settings stay in the browser (IndexedDB `vinyl-db`, localStorage keys `vinyl-prefs`, `vinyl-tracks`, `vinyl-deck`, `vinyl-eq`, `vinyl-eq-presets`).

URL switches: `?demo` loads three synthesized tracks, `?selftest` runs the built-in assertions, `?debug` exposes the deck state as `window.__deck`.
